question: What is the y-intercept of the line that passes through the points (3, 6) and (-1, -5)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Slope (m) = Change in y / Change in x = (−5 − 6) / (−1 − 3) = −11 / −4 = 11/4

Equation of line: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

To find y-intercept, set x = 0: y − 6 = (11/4)(0 − 3)

y = 6 − 33/4 = (24 − 33) / 4 = −9/4

**∴ The correct answer is −9/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Point A = (x₁, y₁) = (3, 6)

Point B = (x₂, y₂) = (−1, −5)

**Formula Used:**

Slope (m) = (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁)

Equation of line: y = mx + c (where c is the y-intercept)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d76f79f106e4eb0ebdcfdb0367f7376db261fbbd7787014402139f1289b93cad.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ m = (−5 − 6) / (−1 − 3)

⇒ m = −11 / −4 = 11/4

⇒ Substitute (3, 6) in y = mx + c:

⇒ 6 = (11/4) × 3 + c

⇒ 6 = 33/4 + c

⇒ c = 6 − 33/4

⇒ c = (24 − 33) / 4

⇒ c = −9/4

**∴ The correct answer is −9/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Slope-Intercept Form

The equation of a straight line is represented as y = mx + c, where m is the slope and c is the y-intercept.

Definition of Y-intercept

The y-intercept is the point where the line crosses the y-axis, calculated by setting x = 0 in the equation.

Two-Point Form

The equation of a line passing through (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is (y − y₁) = [(y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)] × (x − x₁).</p
